findings.where: First screen, the hero's ground (desktop and phone): the band behind the heading, paragraphs, margin notes and photograph
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pale blue-to-lavender-pink wash, not on the warm paper the rest of the page uses. The tile's own palette section says 'A warm paper… Three colours, no accent', so the first screen breaks the system the page presents. The pastel gradient is also the stock look of a software start-up's hero. It brings a pink-violet that is neither the house blue nor the house grey, and it leaves the grey photograph sitting on a cool coloured field instead of on paper.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and asked for every tile to be built in or around #0070C0 and #404040, with one soft ground and the house colours as the only ink. The brief also fails a look any consultancy (or app) could own. A development-bank officer would read it as a tech product's page, not a legal advisor's brief.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph under the heading ('I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…'), desktop and phone
findings.fault: Mark's personal introduction is set as four lines of tracked, bold capitals (eight on phone). After the heading it is the loudest block on the screen, louder than the action and the photograph. All-caps at this length reads as a shouted banner or corporate label, not a man speaking in the first person, and it breaks the quiet legal-journal setting the direction calls for.
findings.who_objects: The founder's personal-advisor test asks that Mark be heard in his own voice, not a firm's tagline, and the brief bans anything that reads as a corporate tagline. A visitor scanning the first screen gets a block that feels like an advertisement strap, not a calm statement from an advisor.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the order of heading, Istanbul note, photograph, caps paragraph, Melbourne note, second paragraph, São Paulo note, then 'Write to me'
findings.fault: On a phone the one action, 'Write to me' with the address, comes only after about one and a half screens of scrolling, below every paragraph and all three margin notes. The first phone screen carries the message and the photo but no way to reach Mark. The margin notes, stacked inline, add three extra stops before the action.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer opening Mark's link from LinkedIn on a phone. The brief asks for one message and one action on the first screen, and here the action is out of sight until they have read everything.

findings.where: First screen, proof beside the action (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Next to 'Write to me', nothing shows who has asked for Mark's work. The paragraph names kinds of body ('multilateral development banks, development agencies and governments') but no named body, role or project. The margin notes give places and years of talks but no host, and they lead nowhere. No third-party proof appears anywhere on the page.
findings.who_objects: The procurement reader (first-visit trust, 'Feel the CV' and item 14) must be sure that Mark has done this kind of work for organisations like theirs before they write. Generic categories of client are what any consultancy claims.

findings.where: First screen and footer: where Mark is based
findings.fault: The page never says what country Mark works from or which regions his advisory work covers. The only places shown are three conference cities, which read as where he spoke, not where he works.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency officer screening consultants against terms of reference that name a region or a base. First-visit trust item 6 asks an international advisor to show the regions of his work.

findings.where: Motion specimen (desktop): the easing curve on the left and the replayed photograph with its timing table on the right
findings.fault: The two columns do not line up. The photo starts halfway down beside the curve, and the table runs on below it beside a large empty block under the curve's caption. The section reads as two unrelated pieces with a hole between them, rather than one sketch of the single entrance it describes.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the specimen parts, which the brief says are judged as part of the candidate. The loose arrangement undercuts the 'placed, settled, still' calm the section claims.
